You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files. Do NOT log in to the live site or hit the live portal. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-08-states-responsive-a11y-terms.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file:line, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. Inventory + diagnosis, no design proposals.

EFFICIENCY: this is mostly grep/count work — use `grep -rn`, `grep -rc`, and `| sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` pipelines, batched in single messages.

CONTEXT FROM COMPLETED SIBLING AUDITS (do not re-derive): there is exactly ONE loading.tsx and ONE error.tsx for all 58 portal routes, both at app/dashboard/; there is no not-found.tsx under /dashboard. There are no toast/dialog/motion libraries in package.json — everything is hand-rolled. Every destructive VPS action uses window.confirm. Five different tab mechanisms coexist. Do NOT re-audit routes or the design-token system; a sibling owns those.

YOUR AUDIT: UI STATES / RESPONSIVE / ACCESSIBILITY / TERMINOLOGY / COPY.
1. LOADING STATES: the single loading.tsx; every skeleton component; every spinner implementation (count distinct); pages that show nothing while loading; long-running action feedback (provisioning overlays, reboot, DNS propagation, payment) and what the user actually sees; Suspense usage; optimistic updates; AutoRefresh/polling components and their intervals.
2. EMPTY STATES: for every list/collection in the portal (servers, games, hosting, sites, domains, mailboxes, volumes, invoices, tickets, activity, team, ssh keys, snapshots, backups, dns records, free-MC, projects, migrations) what the empty state shows (text + CTA + illustration) and how many distinct implementations exist.
3. ERROR STATES: the single error.tsx; error boundaries; how API/action errors surface (toast? inline? alert? thrown?); the actual error copy (grep 'Something went wrong', 'Failed to', 'error' strings) and whether errors say what happened / why / how to fix; retry affordances; 'technical details' disclosure; what a customer sees when a server action fails; 404 handling inside the portal.
4. SUCCESS STATES: after create/deploy/pay/save — toast, redirect, inline, or nothing; any celebration effects.
5. TOASTS / NOTIFICATIONS / BANNERS: how many notification mechanisms exist (hand-rolled toast? inline result boxes? the notification bell? banners?), their variants and positions; every banner type (promo, unverified email, impersonation, overdue, degraded chat, maintenance).
6. MODALS / DRAWERS / DIALOGS: every implementation and count; focus trapping; Escape/overlay close; how many use window.confirm / window.prompt instead of a real dialog (count and list them); whether confirmations state what happens, what is lost, and reversibility; typed-confirm patterns.
7. RESPONSIVE: Shell behaviour below lg (drawer), tables on mobile (overflow-x vs stacked cards — count min-w-[...] on tables), wizards/checkout on mobile, server/hosting panel tabs on mobile, charts on mobile, the terminal/console and file manager on mobile, fixed-width hazards (grep min-w-, w-[NNNpx], grid-cols-N without a breakpoint prefix), touch-target sizes. List the specific pages most likely to break and why.
8. ACCESSIBILITY: counts of aria-*, role=, aria-label; icon-only buttons WITHOUT an accessible name (list them); focus-visible styling; keyboard support in custom dropdowns/tabs/menus/command palette; prefers-reduced-motion handling; colour-contrast risk (list the text utilities used for secondary/muted text and the surface colours they sit on, and estimate which fail AA); form label association (count label htmlFor / aria-labelledby vs input/select/textarea); skip links; heading order; img without alt; live regions (aria-live) for async status.
9. TERMINOLOGY: build a glossary of every user-facing noun for the same concept and where each appears — server/VPS/instance/machine/node; game server/game; hosting/website/site/project/app/plan/account; domain/DNS/zone; mailbox/inbox/email/Business Email; plan/tier/package/size; region/location/node/datacenter; snapshot/backup/image; deploy/order/create/launch/provision/buy/checkout; team/org/workspace; wallet/balance/credits/funds. Note internal jargon leaking to customers (Proxmox, Mailcow, name.com, vmid, node IDs, worker, job, prisma). Note CTA label inconsistencies (Continue/Next/Deploy/Order/Buy/Pay/Place order).
10. COPY TONE: sample ~20 headings/subheads/CTAs across pages to characterise tone inconsistency; any placeholder/TODO/lorem copy; any customer-facing copy implying a third-party infrastructure provider exists (Nxeon must speak as the owner — flag these); NOTE: the '47 seconds' tagline is an intentional brand line, do NOT flag it.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~12-line summary with key counts.

**Summary (audit 08 — states / responsive / a11y / terminology / copy):**

1. **Loading:** 1 `loading.tsx` (generic 4-stat-card skeleton shown for Mail, Terminal, Invoices alike, and it uses `bg-slate-800/*` not the portal's surfaces), 1 Suspense boundary, 5 skeleton impls + ~12 inline, ~6 distinct spinner markups with no shared component. The real loading affordance is a text swap: **~35 distinct pending verbs** plus 26 buttons that just say `"…"`.
2. **Polling:** 9 `AutoRefresh` mounts (5 s route refresh) + **29 `setInterval`** across 8 different intervals; none back off or pause on hidden tabs, and several stack on the same page.
3. **Empty states:** **6 implementations** (~40 collections). One shared primitive (24 uses) with a single generic server-rack SVG for Domains/Invoices/Tickets/Sites/Mail alike; only ~6 of ~40 offer a CTA. Two feature-flag empties leak internal state ("once this feature is configured").
4. **Errors:** one boundary, copy is "Something went wrong" ×11 with a `ref:` digest rendered in `text-slate-600` (~2.5:1). **5 competing error mechanisms**, including **10 `window.alert()` — all in shared hosting**, and 27 swallowed catches. **No `/dashboard/not-found.tsx`**, so 8 `notFound()` calls dump the customer onto the marketing 404 outside the shell.
5. **Modals:** 28 overlays / 24 files, **zero focus traps**, 9 of 24 handle Escape, 15 `role="dialog"`. **60 `window.confirm`, 9 `window.prompt`, 3 different typed-confirm patterns**; ~13 confirms say nothing beyond "Delete this X?".
6. **Responsive:** Shell/drawer is genuinely well done (`inert`, Escape, `--nx-rail-w`). Tables are not: 41 tables, **zero stacked-card variants**, `min-w-[980px]` on Domains, and 15 tables with neither `min-w` nor an overflow wrapper (incl. server Networking/Firewall). Worst offenders: Domains, servers/[id] Networking+Console (`Console.tsx:206` has no responsive handling at all), DB Studio, `grid-cols-9 w-fit` inventory grids. 8 tab strips split 5 `overflow-x-auto` / 3 `flex-wrap`.
7. **A11y — biggest finding: `text-slate-500` is used 694 times and fails AA (~4.0:1) on navy**, and it's baked into `.section-label`, every `.table-shell` header, and every input placeholder; `text-slate-600` (81) fails even AA-large. Also: **133 of 219 labels (61%) have no programmatic association**, 3 `aria-live` total (ProvisioningOverlay is silent for minutes), **no skip link**, **no global focus style** (`focus-visible:` appears 3 times), 9 genuinely unnamed icon-only buttons, **no blanket `prefers-reduced-motion` rule** (page-transition `animate-fade-up`, all skeletons and spinners animate regardless), and the whole Deploy/checkout funnel has no `h1`.
8. **Terminology:** **6 nouns for a VPS** (server / VPS / virtual machine / instance / box / VM — four of them on adjacent screens), **10 verbs for "buy"**, Team↔organization↔org↔workspace↔roster, wallet↔balance↔funds↔credit, and the nav's own comment renames "Business email"→"Mailboxes" while `email/page.tsx:70` still titles it "Business Email". Deploy step is labelled "Location" but its own reassurance string says "node".
9. **Jargon leak:** "hypervisor" appears in **10 customer-facing strings**, plus "nginx" ×3, "worker job", "relay", "document root". Proxmox/Mailcow/vmid/prisma stay internal.
10. **Brand voice:** **6 strings to fix** that imply an outside infra provider for something Nxeon owns — notably `EmailDnsSetup.tsx:125,138` ("at your registrar"/"your DNS provider" for Nxeon-registered domains) and `GameCustomDomain.tsx:184` which names Cloudflare/GoDaddy/Namecheap and omits Nxeon Domains. The migration-wizard "old provider" strings are legitimate and not flagged; "47 seconds" does not appear in the portal.
11. **Copy tone:** five registers coexist (plain-utility, technical-boast, marketing-in-portal, warm-conversational, bare fragments); title case and subhead punctuation are inconsistent; 5 hand-rolled "coming soon" treatments while an unused `ComingSoon` primitive exists.
12. **Duplication:** identical confirm strings written twice in two files (×3 cases), the suspended-server banner rendered twice on one page, and two different heroes on `/dashboard/partner`.
